The test image shows a corn ear with white/grayish-white fluffy mold growth on the kernels, with some kernel damage/discoloration in the affected area. This is clearly an ear rot disease. Top candidates: Diplodia_Ear_Rot, Fusarium_Disease, Gibberella_Disease, Trichoderma_Ear_Rot.

Let me check reference images one at a time.
Now checking remaining classes to cover 16 different classes as required.

I've now checked 16 reference images across 14 different classes. Let me summarize my analysis:

**Test image key features:**
- Corn ear (not leaf/stalk)
- White/grayish-white fluffy mold concentrated in a band across the middle section of the ear
- Kernels in the affected area appear damaged/brownish
- Healthy yellow kernels on either side of the affected zone

**Comparison to references:**
- **Fusarium_Disease** (Corn_Disease_25): Very close match — white/gray mold patches on a section of ear kernels with surrounding healthy yellow kernels. Same general appearance.
- **Diplodia_Ear_Rot**: Tends to show denser white mycelium starting from the base, often covering the whole ear. Cross-section shows black pycnidia. Less similar.
- **Gibberella_Disease**: Pink/reddish mold at tip — no pink visible in test image.
- **Trichoderma_Ear_Rot**: Green/blue-green mold covering entire ear — no match.
- **Aspergillus_Ear_Rot**: Olive-green powdery mold — no match.
- **Common_Smut**: Black galls — no match.
- All leaf/stalk diseases (NLB, GLS, Rust, Tar Spot, etc.): Wrong plant part entirely.

The white/gray mold concentrated in a mid-section band with surrounding healthy kernels is most consistent with Fusarium ear rot, matching particularly well with Corn_Disease_25.
